It is a sidecar rather than a `_comment` key inside each fixture because these bodies are meant to be byte-faithful: a client that parses one must see exactly what the API sends, and an extra key would be a lie in the shape of documentation. `python3 frontend/verify_fixtures.py` re-derives every claim below from the source and fails if one has gone stale.

_searches._comment: Task 25's six routes, frozen 2026-08-02. Eleven files: two list scopes plus an empty one, a request and a response for POST, one by-id, a watch/unwatch pair, and three results pages. They replace nothing -- fixtures/contract/ASPIRATIONAL_*_searches.* stay where they are, because they describe a shape that was never built and the deviation list between the two is an artifact somebody has to be able to read. See ../contract/MANIFEST.json and ../../README.md § 'Where the search contract and the shipped API differ'.
_searches._role_track_means_two_different_things_i: AND THIS IS THE NOTE TO READ BEFORE WRITING ANY COPY. On a JOB row (GET_v1_searches_results.json, GET_v1_jobs.json) `role_track` is job_facts.role_track -- the posting's family, the axis tracks.mjs groups Today by, one of extract.ROLE_TRACK's nine. On a QUERY object (every other search fixture here) `role_track` is search_queries.role_track -- the track a SEEDED suggestion was generated from, i.e. why that row exists at all. Same closed vocabulary, two different subjects, and they NEVER share a JSON object: a query object carries no posting fields and a job row carries no query fields. Nothing structural stops the two being conflated -- only the copy does, which is why the client says 'For roles like: …' on a suggestion and renders no track heading at all over search results.
_searches._watcher_bucket_is_null_or_a_label_and_n: The single most misreadable field in these fixtures, and a sharper case than cohort_signal's. search_query_signal.watcher_bucket is NOT NULL and the row is ABSENT below schema.SEARCH_MIN_WATCHERS = 4, so the LEFT JOIN in search._SIGNAL_JOIN yields null for 0, 1, 2 AND 3 watchers indistinguishably. A client must render null as NO BADGE -- never a zero, never a greyed dash, never 'fewer than four', never 'be the first'. The floor is 4 where cohort_signal's is 3 for two reasons DEC-85 sets out and neither applies to a save count: the observed object is ATTACKER-CHOSEN (anyone can create the query they want to watch the bucket of, which is a chosen-plaintext capability), and THE PLANTER IS ALWAYS A WATCHER (POST /v1/searches registers its caller, so a floor of 3 gives an anonymity set of two). The labels are '4-6' / '7-10' / '11+' and deliberately do not overlap, unlike COHORT_BUCKETS' '3-5' / '6-10' / '10+'. At today's cohort size -- two labellers, git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/labelling-report-2026-08-02.md -- EVERY value is null, so null is the case the UI has to handle well, not the edge case. One fixture row carries '4-6' so a client author sees the populated shape once.
_searches._what_is_deliberately_absent: first_requested_at is NOT in QUERY_COLUMNS and its absence is the point rather than an oversight: it is the timestamp at which one identifiable person typed something, and timing is the strongest deanonymiser available in a cohort who sit in a room together (search.py's module docstring, tranche_five/28). last_run_at IS exposed, because that is the pipeline's clock and no person's act. search_query_signal.computed_at is not selected either, for the same reason jobs._COHORT_COLUMNS refuses it: a per-row timestamp that moves when the underlying set moves is the recency channel the bucketing exists to close. And there is no watcher_count anywhere -- DEC-87, the count is a separate table precisely so the service cannot write one. verify_fixtures.py fails on any of the four appearing in a fixture.

notes: THE SHAPE IS /v1/jobs' SHAPE, FIELD FOR FIELD, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A search result list is a rendered list, position bias applies to it identically, and tranche_five/27's instrumentation is unusable if half the renders in the product report positions in a different vocabulary. Every column, join and field name is imported, so the two lists cannot drift into two shapes -- a client rendering both would then need two renderers for one kind of thing. The rows here are the same three postings as GET_v1_jobs.json, which is what lets check_client.mjs assert ui.jobCard produces identical output from either source.

THE JOIN IS THE GATE. A posting appears only if match.py wrote it a job_matches row, which it does only for postings passing relevance.union_sql, and only if it satisfies jobs_app's four completeness predicates. Google Jobs is precisely where the relister junk originates -- config/relevance.json already carries six excluded relist sites and a description_exclude for the 'reputed company' placeholder BECAUSE this source fed them in. A route that read `jobs` directly would surface the exact postings the curated pipeline exists to suppress, to people with no industry pattern-matching to catch it.

`query_id` is echoed and is the ONLY thing this envelope says about the query -- not its text, not its watch state, not whether it has ever run. A client needs GET /v1/searches/{id} as well to render a heading, and that is not a wasted round trip.

The events validator threads a real one through because it has a batch to name; a rejected search submission belongs to no render.

too_many_searches is the cap searchnorm.MAX_QUERIES_PER_BUILDER = 20 enforces, counted over WATCHES rather than over rows created -- a Builder watching twenty searches other people created spends the same nightly quota as one who typed twenty. So the remedy in the message is 'stop watching one', not 'delete one'.
